decision.summary: Hot water has been out since 6 May on a landlord-arranged route. The landlord says his plumber fixed it on 14 May, with no evidence, and the tenant has not confirmed. I logged the letterbox report as its own job, wrote to the tenant by letter, texted the landlord for details and consent to send our contractor if needed, and put the job on hold to 19 May.

answers.question: Where does this case stand and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Open and unverified. Landlord says fixed on 14 May via his plumber (no name, report or invoice); tenant's latest word is no hot water and she has not replied to the voicemail or email of 15 May. Outstanding: tenant confirmation, plumber details, cause of the power fault, and the letterbox (now JOB-101).

answers.question: What is the next action, who for, which channel?
answers.answer: Letter to tenant Iris Vale asking her to confirm status (A3), as email and a call went unanswered. SMS to landlord Ravi Sethi asking for plumber details and consent to send our contractor (A4). Hold with review on 19 May (A5).

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision?
answers.answer: Not yet. If the tenant says there is still no hot water on 19 May, or the landlord does not reply, escalate P2 maintenance and send our contractor.

args.body: Dear Iris, we are sorry about the long wait for hot water. Your landlord says his plumber attended on 14 May and fixed it, but we have not heard from you since, so we are not treating it as fixed. Please tell us: is hot water working now, and does the boiler have power? If not, reply and we will press the landlord today and arrange our own contractor as a back-up. If anyone at home feels unwell or is struggling, tell us. We have also logged your letterbox problem as a separate job (JOB-101); please tell us what is wrong with it. We will contact you again on Monday 19 May. A reply by email, portal or phone to us is fine.
